label: CERBERUS walkthrough: letting the question decide how much of an image to read

steps.title: Today a model reads every patch, whatever you ask.
steps.text: A vision-language model answers questions about a picture. It first cuts the picture into small squares called patches. Its language part then reads every patch, even for an easy question.
steps.gridLabel: A simple scene cut into a grid of patches. Every patch is highlighted.

steps.title: The idea: let the question choose how many patches to read.
steps.text: A narrow question needs only a few patches. A broad one needs many. Pick a question to see which patches would be read.
steps.counterLabel: Patches the language model would read:

questions.gridLabel: Only the patches around the sign are highlighted.

steps.title: What I built first: images and words in one shared space.
steps.text: In a shared space, a picture and the words that describe it land close together, like nearby points on one map.
steps.alt: Two scatter plots of image and text embeddings. In the left plot, image dots and text crosses are interleaved. In the right plot, they sit in separate clusters.
steps.caption: Each dot is a picture and each cross is a caption, flattened onto a page. Left, the version I built: pictures and captions mix together. Right, the Perceiver try: they stay apart.

steps.title: That shared space can be shrunk.
steps.text: Each picture becomes a list of numbers, called a vector. I trained it so the front part works alone, like nesting dolls. Pick a size.
steps.vectorLabel: The vector as a row of cells. Solid cells are kept, dashed cells are cut off.
steps.metricGloss: How often the right caption is among the top five matches. Paired PixMo validation set, early measurement.
steps.caption: This shrinks the vector, not the number of patches.

steps.title: What is next, and what did not work.
steps.text: Select a part to read where it stands.

chips.name: Question-aware selector
chips.text: A small module that reads the question and decides how many patches reach the language model. It is planned, not built.

chips.name: Qwen decoder with LoRA
chips.statusText: Partial, one run, no held-out answer metric yet
chips.text: A Qwen language model, tuned with LoRA (small add-on weights), was trained once at 7 billion parameters. Only the training loss was tracked, with no answer score on held-out questions yet.

chips.name: Perceiver compression
chips.text: Squeezing the image into a few tokens with a Perceiver was tried, but finding the right caption stayed near random chance.

more.summary: More detail on how it is built

items.name: Image encoder
items.text: a frozen CLIP model turns the picture into patch features and is never retrained.

items.name: Text encoder
items.text: a frozen sentence encoder turns the caption into numbers.

items.name: Attention pooling
items.text: a small learned layer squeezes the patch features into one vector in the shared space.

items.name: Nested resizable vectors (Matryoshka)
items.text: the front part of the vector works on its own, like nesting dolls.

items.name: Contrastive alignment
items.text: training on PixMo image-caption pairs pulls each picture toward its own caption and away from the others.
